.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/task: every file (task.toml, instruction.md, environment/Dockerfile, environment/instructions/*.md, environment/assets/kittle.json, solution/solve.sh, solution/app/{package.json,server.js,seed/kittle.json,public/*}, tests/* incl. all judge.toml/prompt.md, app_context.md, Dockerfiles, .dockerignore) via full-tree grep for URLs, host paths, key shapes, PEM, password/token/secret, emails, prompt-injection phrases, plus full read of the seed JSON
evidence: No live credential, real personal data, host path or unpinned code fetch found; one deliberate, publicly required XSS fixture sits in the seed, which a literal reading of 'injection payload anywhere' could flag. (1) Credentials: task.toml:34 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" (template, not a literal), task.toml:35 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "". No sk-/AKIA/ghp_/xox/PEM shapes anywhere. Only password is the documented demo 'password123' (environment/instructions/walls-and-retention.md:3, tests/app_context.md:8, solution/app/server.js:17), which the SKILL profile and Deterministic row 19 explicitly allow. (2) Personal data: seed environment/assets/kittle.json (sha256 42ab8b97..., identical to solution/app/seed/kittle.json) uses fictional firm 'Kittle & Rowe', generic names (Harriet Rowe, Dev Anand, Sian Lloyd, Gwen Pryce, Paul Marsh) on the reserved .test TLD; the only other email is turing@local.invalid in the template Dockerfile. No phone numbers, addresses or IDs. (3) Host paths: none. Only container paths /tmp/submission (template test.sh:6), /assets/kittle.json fallback (server.js:29), /app, /instructions. No F:/, C:\, /home, /Users. (4) Remote fetch: environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template; npm packages pinned exactly (express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79), pip harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, package.json exact versions. Base images are tag-not-digest (node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.12-slim) and apt is unpinned, but that is template-controlled and must be preserved. No curl/wget/CDN; solution index.html loads only /styles.css and /app.js; server.js requires only crypto/fs/path/express/better-sqlite3. URLs in task: localhost/127.0.0.1, https://openrouter.ai/api (frozen verifier block), and https://example.org/lease (IANA-reserved) as message text in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:164 graded only as 'a link that opens in a new tab' (row-25 concern at most, not a fetch dependency). (5) Injection: no prompt-injection text aimed at the judge (grep for ignore/disregard/system prompt/you are/score etc. in seed, instructions, app_context: none). However seed message K-16 (environment/assets/kittle.json, M-11) body is 'Pasted from the lease: Schedule 2 On hold [link](javascript:alert(2))', and judge.toml:164 has the judge post ' [click](javascript:alert(9))'. These are benign alert() probes backing a public requirement (environment/instructions/conversations.md:13: 'Anything else that looks like markup, scripts or HTML is just text and shows exactly as it was typed, everywhere a message appears') and graded by safe_formatting (judge.toml:160-168, with positive controls). I judge this a legitimate escaping test fixture, not a malicious payload or a defect; it does not exfiltrate, target the judge's reasoning, or touch the host. Risk is set true only because the workbook text says 'injection payload anywhere in the task' and quality-checks.md #12 says 'free-text fields carry no injection payload', so a literal hosted reviewer could flag K-16; this is unmeasured (no hosted QC run). Weak-app probe: an app that renders K-16 via innerHTML would fire alert(1) in the judge's browser; that is exactly what safe_formatting is designed to fail, and Playwright MCP surfaces the dialog, so the fixture discriminates rather than endangering grading. Conforming-alternative probe: an app that escapes everything is unaffected by the fixture. Raw evidence index present (sha256 64571a08...); no runtime evidence is needed for this static row.
suggested_fix: Optional, no defect: if hosted QC flags K-16, add a one-line author note (e.g. in the delivery notes, not the brief) that K-16 and the safe_formatting text are inert alert() escaping fixtures for conversations.md:13; do not remove them, since they back a scored public requirement. Strip nothing else; task.toml already uses ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}.
